title: LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS AS TOOLS FOR PUBLIC BUILDING ENERGY MANAGEMENT: AN ASSESSMENT OF POSSIBILITIES AND BARRIERS

live_model.evidence: "the study employed GPT-3.5 ... and GPT-4 Turbo (trained on data up until December 2023, Context window 128000 tokens)" (Sec. 2, analysis conducted "second half of April 2024")

prompt.note: 4 fixed questions asked once per country (Serbia, Poland) via the chat interface; no system prompt or API parameters given.

claim.metric: mean overestimation of fenestration U-value vs. ground truth, Serbia construction period I
claim.location: Sec. 3.3 discussion (Republic of Serbia results), Table 6/Figure 3

data.source: National building-typology reports for Serbia (Popovic et al. 2018) and Poland (Polish National Energy Conservation Agency 2012); the 4 questions are printed in the paper

notes: Only 4 questions x 2 countries were asked (n items are single point-estimates, not a scoreable dataset); no API, temperature, or token-parameter details are given anywhere, and the 'chat bot' framing throughout indicates manual use of the ChatGPT web interface rather than the API. GPT-4-turbo timing (analysis in second half of April 2024) is right at the 2024-04-09 GA date with no preview string, so gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 is the best-supported resolution though not fully inside the SCHEMA's after-2024-07-01 window.
